questions.explain: Management review considers the status of previous actions, changes in issues and in interested parties' needs, performance information including nonconformities, monitoring and audit results, and improvement opportunities. Invoices and raw source code are not management review inputs.

questions.stem: A model was deployed without its required validation sign-off. Put the clause 10.2 response steps in order.
options: React: control and correct the nonconformity, for example roll back the model
Determine the root cause and whether similar nonconformities exist
Implement the corrective action needed
Review the effectiveness of the corrective action
Update the AIMS if necessary and retain documented information
questions.explain: Clause 10.2 requires reacting to the nonconformity, evaluating the need for action by finding the cause and checking for similar cases, implementing corrective action, reviewing its effectiveness and making changes to the AIMS if needed. The nonconformity and actions are recorded as documented information.

questions.case: Internal audit finds that three recent model releases skipped the fairness test. The team re-runs the tests on all three models and closes the finding.
questions.stem: Why is this response incomplete under ISO/IEC 42001?
options: Fairness testing is not part of 42001, so no finding should have been raised
Only the certification body may close audit findings
Re-running the tests is a correction, but the root cause of the skipped gate has not been found and removed
The models must be withdrawn permanently after any nonconformity
questions.explain: Re-running the tests fixes the immediate problem, which is a correction. Corrective action under 10.2 requires finding and removing the cause, such as a bypassable pipeline, and then checking that it worked. Organizations close their own internal findings, and permanent withdrawal is not required.

questions.stem: In a two-stage initial certification audit for ISO/IEC 42001, what does the stage 2 audit mainly evaluate?
options: Whether the organization has paid the certification fee
Whether the AIMS scope document has been written
Whether the organization has selected a certification body
Whether the AIMS is implemented and effective in practice
questions.explain: Stage 1 reviews documentation and readiness, such as the scope, policy and SoA. Stage 2 evaluates implementation and effectiveness by sampling records, interviewing staff and observing practice. Fees and choosing a certification body are administrative steps, not audit stages.

questions.stem: For each statement about documented information in ISO/IEC 42001, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Results of AI system impact assessments must be retained as documented information.
If staff perform internal audits but keep no records, the audit requirement is still met.
Management review results are retained as evidence.

questions.explain: 42001 requires retained documented information for impact assessment results, the audit programme and audit results, and management review results, among others. Without records an auditor has no evidence, so an unrecorded audit fails clause 9.2's documentation requirement.

questions.stem: Put the typical ISO/IEC 42001 certification life cycle in order.
options: Stage 1 audit of documentation and readiness
Stage 2 audit of implementation and effectiveness
Certificate issued
Periodic surveillance audits
Recertification audit before the certificate cycle ends
questions.explain: Initial certification is a stage 1 readiness review followed by a stage 2 effectiveness audit. After the certificate is issued, surveillance audits confirm continued conformity, and recertification renews the cycle, which typically lasts three years.

questions.stem: How many reference controls does Annex A of ISO/IEC 42001:2023 contain?
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A lists 38 controls across nine areas, A.2 to A.10. 93 is the number of controls in ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, and 114 was the number in ISO/IEC 27001:2013. 72 is not an Annex A control count.

questions.stem: For each statement about ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Annex A is normative.
Every Annex A control must be implemented, whatever the risk assessment says.
Excluding an Annex A control requires a justification in the Statement of Applicability.

questions.explain: Annex A is normative, but controls are selected through AI risk treatment. The SoA records the necessary controls and justifies including or excluding each Annex A control. The organization may also add controls that are not in Annex A.

questions.stem: A data scientist wants a confidential way to raise concerns that a model is being used in ways it was not validated for. Which ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A control does this BEST map to?
options: A.8.3 External reporting
A.3.3 Reporting of concerns
A.8.4 Communication of incidents
A.2.4 Review of the AI policy
questions.explain: A.3.3 requires a process for people in the organization to report concerns about its role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle. A.8.3 lets external interested parties report adverse impacts. A.8.4 covers communicating incidents to users, and A.2.4 covers reviewing the AI policy.

questions.stem: Which resource types are covered by controls in area A.4, Resources for AI systems? Select THREE.
options: Data resources
Tooling resources
System and computing resources
Marketing resources
Legal privilege resources
questions.explain: A.4 includes resource documentation (A.4.2), data resources (A.4.3), tooling resources (A.4.4), system and computing resources (A.4.5) and human resources (A.4.6). Marketing and legal privilege are not Annex A resource categories.

questions.stem: An impact assessment for a news-recommendation AI considers its potential effect on public discourse and the spread of misinformation. Which Annex A control does this MOST directly address?
options: A.5.4 Assessing AI system impact on individuals or groups of individuals
A.7.4 Quality of data for AI systems
A.5.5 Assessing societal impacts of AI systems
A.9.4 Intended use of the AI system
questions.explain: Effects on public discourse and misinformation are society-wide, which is A.5.5. A.5.4 covers impacts on specific individuals or groups, such as discrimination against a user group. Data quality (A.7.4) and intended use (A.9.4) are related, but they are not impact assessment controls.

questions.stem: A team confirms that a credit model meets its documented requirements and is fit for its intended lending use before release. Which Annex A control covers this activity?
options: A.6.2.6 AI system operation and monitoring
A.6.2.8 AI system recording of event logs
A.7.6 Data preparation
A.6.2.4 AI system verification and validation
questions.explain: Checking that requirements are met (verification) and that the system is fit for its intended use (validation) is A.6.2.4. Operation and monitoring (A.6.2.6) happens after deployment, event logging (A.6.2.8) records system events, and data preparation (A.7.6) covers cleaning and labelling data.

questions.stem: Under control A.6.2.8, at what point in the life cycle must event logging of an AI system be enabled as a minimum?
options: During data acquisition only
While the AI system is in use
Only during verification and validation
Only after an incident has occurred
questions.explain: A.6.2.8 asks the organization to decide at which life cycle phases event logs are recorded, and at a minimum this includes when the AI system is in use. Logging only during acquisition or testing, or only after an incident, would lose the operational traceability the control aims for.

questions.case: Six months after launch, a demand-forecasting model's accuracy falls steadily as customer behaviour shifts. Nobody notices until quarterly results are missed. The model had passed validation before deployment.
questions.stem: Which Annex A control was MOST likely implemented ineffectively?
options: A.6.2.6 AI system operation and monitoring
A.6.2.4 AI system verification and validation
A.10.3 Suppliers
A.2.3 Alignment with other organizational policies
questions.explain: The model was valid at release but drifted in production without detection. That is a failure of operation and monitoring (A.6.2.6), which covers ongoing performance monitoring, repairs and updates. Validation (A.6.2.4) passed, and suppliers and policy alignment are not involved.

questions.stem: Which Annex A control requires an organization to record the origin of data used in its AI systems and how that data has changed across the life cycle?
options: A.7.4 Quality of data for AI systems
A.7.3 Acquisition of data
A.7.6 Data preparation
A.7.5 Data provenance
questions.explain: Data provenance (A.7.5) means recording where data came from and how it was processed over the data and AI system life cycles. A.7.3 covers how data is acquired and selected, A.7.4 covers data quality requirements, and A.7.6 covers the methods used to prepare data.

questions.stem: Which TWO controls belong to area A.8, Information for interested parties of AI systems? Select TWO.
options: Communication of incidents
Reporting of concerns
External reporting
Allocating responsibilities
Intended use of the AI system
questions.explain: A.8 contains system documentation and information for users (A.8.2), external reporting (A.8.3), communication of incidents (A.8.4) and information for interested parties (A.8.5). Reporting of concerns is A.3.3, allocating responsibilities is A.10.2 and intended use is A.9.4.

questions.case: Members of the public say a city's AI chatbot gives them wrong information about benefit eligibility. They have no way to tell the city. Separately, a training-data audit shows that 30% of records have missing income fields.
questions.stem: Which pair of Annex A controls MOST directly addresses these two gaps?
options: A.3.3 Reporting of concerns, and A.7.5 Data provenance
A.8.3 External reporting, and A.7.4 Quality of data for AI systems
A.8.2 System documentation for users, and A.7.3 Acquisition of data
A.5.5 Societal impacts, and A.4.3 Data resources
questions.explain: Giving outside parties a way to report adverse impacts is A.8.3. Missing fields are a data quality problem, which is A.7.4. A.3.3 is an internal channel, and provenance tracks origin rather than completeness. User documentation, acquisition, societal assessment and resource documentation do not close these specific gaps.

questions.stem: Staff begin using an AI summarization tool, approved for internal meeting notes, to draft legal advice for clients. Which Annex A control is MOST directly at issue?
options: A.6.2.2 AI system requirements and specification
A.10.4 Customers
A.9.4 Intended use of the AI system
A.4.6 Human resources
questions.explain: A.9.4 requires the AI system to be used according to its intended use and documentation. Drafting client legal advice goes well beyond the approved use. Requirements specification (A.6.2.2), customer expectations (A.10.4) and human resources (A.4.6) do not directly address use outside the approved purpose.

questions.stem: A company builds products on a third-party foundation model. For each statement about Annex A area A.10, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Responsibilities across the AI life cycle should be allocated between the company and the model supplier.
The company should have a process so that what suppliers provide aligns with its responsible AI approach.
Because the model is external, A.10 lets the company transfer all accountability to the supplier.

questions.explain: A.10.2 requires responsibilities to be allocated among the organization, partners, suppliers and customers, and A.10.3 requires supplier offerings to align with the organization's responsible AI approach. Using an external model does not remove the organization's accountability for its own AIMS.

questions.stem: Where would an implementer find guidance on how to implement each ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A control?
options: ISO/IEC 27002
Annex B of ISO/IEC 42001
Annex D of ISO/IEC 42001
ISO/IEC 22989
questions.explain: Annex B of 42001 gives implementation guidance for each Annex A control. ISO/IEC 27002 is the guidance for ISO/IEC 27001 controls, Annex D covers use across domains and sectors, and ISO/IEC 22989 defines AI terminology.

questions.stem: A risk workshop wants a starting list of AI risk sources, such as 'level of automation' and 'technology readiness'. Which part of ISO/IEC 42001 provides this?
options: Annex A
Clause 6.2
Annex C
Annex B
questions.explain: Informative Annex C lists potential AI-related organizational objectives and risk sources, including level of automation, technology readiness, complexity of environment and machine learning-specific risk sources. Annex A lists controls, Annex B gives control guidance, and clause 6.2 sets requirements for AI objectives.

questions.stem: Which statement BEST describes how an AI system impact assessment differs from an AI risk assessment in ISO/IEC 42001?
options: Impact assessment focuses on people and society; risk assessment weighs risks to AI objectives against criteria
Impact assessment is optional, while risk assessment is mandatory
Impact assessment covers only financial losses to the organization
Impact assessment replaces risk assessment for high-risk systems
questions.explain: 42001 requires both processes. The impact assessment (6.1.4) is centred on people and society. The risk assessment (6.1.2) evaluates risks to the organization's AI objectives against its criteria, and impact results feed into it. Neither replaces the other, and impact is not limited to financial loss.

questions.case: A recruitment platform's AI risk assessment rates its CV-ranking model as low risk, because complaints are rare and the contracts limit liability. A later analysis shows candidates over 50 are ranked lower far more often.
questions.stem: Which process should have surfaced this harm, and what should happen with the finding?
options: Internal audit, which should raise a minor nonconformity only
Management review, which should update the AI policy only
Supplier evaluation under A.10.3, which should end the contract
The AI system impact assessment, whose results should feed into AI risk assessment and treatment
questions.explain: Harm to a group of individuals is what the impact assessment is designed to surface, even when organizational risk looks low. Its results feed AI risk assessment and treatment, for example bias mitigation or human review. Audit, management review and supplier evaluation are not the primary mechanisms.

questions.stem: Which factors should an AI system impact assessment take into account? Select THREE.
options: Reasonably foreseeable misuse of the system
The jurisdictions where the system will be deployed
The technical and societal context of the system
The vendor's share price
The number of ISO standards the organization holds
questions.explain: Impact assessments consider intended use and reasonably foreseeable misuse, the specific technical and societal context, and the jurisdictions of deployment. A vendor's share price and the organization's other certificates say nothing about consequences for people.

questions.case: A company built a voice-cloning feature for audiobook narrators. Its impact assessment covers only narrators using their own voices with consent. The feature will launch in four countries next quarter.
questions.stem: What is the MOST important weakness in this impact assessment?
options: It should have been done by the certification body
It ignores foreseeable misuse, such as cloning others' voices for fraud, and differences between jurisdictions
It should cover only the country with the largest market
It should cover only data quality, not the use of the feature
questions.explain: Looking only at intended use misses foreseeable misuse such as impersonation and fraud, and ignores the different legal and social context in each deployment country. The organization performs its own assessment, and limiting it to one country or to data quality would make it narrower still.

questions.stem: For each statement about AI system impact assessment results under ISO/IEC 42001, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Results are documented and retained.
Results can be an input to AI risk assessment and risk treatment.
Every impact assessment must be published in full on the organization's website.

questions.explain: Clauses 6.1.4 and 8.4 and control A.5.3 require results to be documented and retained, and they feed into risk assessment and treatment. Sharing with interested parties is decided where appropriate. 42001 does not require full public publication of every assessment.

questions.stem: Which standard gives guidance specifically on how to carry out an AI system impact assessment?
options: ISO/IEC 42006
ISO/IEC 23894
ISO/IEC 17021-1
ISO/IEC 42005
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 42005:2025 gives guidance on assessing the impacts of AI systems on individuals, groups and society. ISO/IEC 23894 gives guidance on AI risk management, ISO/IEC 42006 sets requirements for AIMS certification bodies, and ISO/IEC 17021-1 covers certification bodies in general.

questions.stem: A company choosing an auditor for its ISO/IEC 42001 certification wants assurance that the auditors have AI-specific competence. Which standard should the certification body operate under?
options: ISO/IEC 42006
ISO/IEC 42005
ISO/IEC 22989
ISO/IEC 23894
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 42006:2025 sets requirements for bodies that audit and certify AI management systems, including AI-specific auditor competence. It builds on ISO/IEC 17021-1. ISO/IEC 42005 and ISO/IEC 23894 are guidance for organizations, and ISO/IEC 22989 is terminology.

questions.stem: ISO/IEC 23894, which supports AI risk assessment under ISO/IEC 42001, adapts which general risk management standard to AI?
options: ISO/IEC 27005
ISO/IEC 27701
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 23894 gives AI-specific guidance based on ISO 31000, Risk management guidelines. ISO/IEC 27005 is information security risk guidance, ISO 22301 covers business continuity, and ISO/IEC 27701 covers privacy information management.

questions.stem: A team is scoping the impact assessment for a large generative AI model trained on huge compute clusters and used by millions of people. Which TWO impact areas are MOST clearly relevant beyond individual privacy? Select TWO.
options: Environmental impact from energy use in training and operation
Office floor-space utilization
Societal effects such as misinformation and information integrity
The model's file format
Brand colour consistency
questions.explain: Typical impact areas include fairness, accountability, transparency, privacy, safety, human rights and the environment. At this scale, energy use (environmental impact, also an Annex C objective) and societal effects such as misinformation are clearly relevant. Floor space, file formats and branding are not AI impact areas.

questions.stem: An ISMS built to ISO/IEC 27001 aims to preserve which three information security properties?
options: Authenticity, accountability and non-repudiation
Confidentiality, integrity and availability
Identification, authentication and authorization
Privacy, safety and resilience
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 27001 frames the ISMS around preserving confidentiality, integrity and availability. Authenticity and non-repudiation are related properties but not the core three. Identification, authentication and authorization describe access control steps. Privacy, safety and resilience are separate concerns.

questions.stem: For each statement about ISO/IEC 27001, select Yes if true.

statements.s: It specifies requirements that an organization's ISMS can be audited and certified against.
It requires every organization to implement all Annex A controls regardless of its risk assessment.
It expects the ISMS to be continually improved rather than set up once.

questions.explain: 27001 contains 'shall' requirements used for certification. Controls are selected based on risk; Annex A controls can be excluded with justification in the SoA. Continual improvement is a core requirement (clause 10.1).

questions.stem: What did ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Amendment 1:2024 change?
options: It added eleven new Annex A controls, including threat intelligence and cloud services security
It added a new clause on planning of changes to the ISMS
It added a climate change consideration to clause 4.1 and a related note to clause 4.2
It made ISO 31000 the mandatory risk assessment method
questions.explain: Amd 1:2024 requires organizations to determine whether climate change is a relevant issue (4.1) and notes interested parties can have climate requirements (4.2). The eleven new controls and clause 6.3 came with the 2022 edition itself. No risk method is mandated.

questions.case: In 2026 an external auditor reviews clause 4 for a certified software company. The context register lists regulatory, technical and staffing issues but contains no evidence that climate change was ever considered. The ISMS manager argues that climate change has nothing to do with information security.
questions.stem: Which response best reflects the current requirements?
options: Climate change is outside the ISMS because ISO/IEC 27001 deals only with information security
The company must add an Annex A control for climate risk to its Statement of Applicability
The company must obtain ISO 14001 certification before its next surveillance audit
It must decide whether climate change is relevant and may conclude that it is not
questions.explain: Since Amd 1:2024, clause 4.1 requires a determination of whether climate change is a relevant issue. Concluding it is not relevant is acceptable if the decision was made. There is no Annex A climate control, and ISO 14001 certification is not required.

questions.stem: By what date did certified organizations have to complete their transition from ISO/IEC 27001:2013 to ISO/IEC 27001:2022?
options: 31 October 2023
30 April 2024
31 October 2025
31 December 2026
questions.explain: The three-year transition period ended on 31 October 2025. 31 October 2023 was a deadline for certification bodies' own accreditation transitions in many schemes, and 30 April 2024 was the date from which new and recertification audits had to use the 2022 edition.

questions.case: A logistics firm holds an accredited ISO/IEC 27001:2013 certificate printed with an expiry date of March 2026. Busy with a system migration, it postponed its transition audit and had not been audited against the 2022 edition by November 2025. A customer now asks whether the certificate is still valid.
questions.stem: What is the most accurate answer?
options: No; 2013 certificates lapsed when the transition period ended on 31 October 2025
Yes; the certificate remains valid until its printed expiry date in March 2026
Yes; it converts automatically to the 2022 edition at the next surveillance audit
Yes, provided the firm's SoA maps the old controls to the 2022 Annex A
questions.explain: Certificates to the 2013 edition ceased to be valid after 31 October 2025 regardless of printed expiry. There is no automatic conversion; a transition or new certification audit by the certification body is required. Mapping controls in the SoA alone does not restore validity.

questions.stem: A security engineer wants detailed implementation guidance for each control listed in ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A. Which standard should they use?
options: ISO/IEC 27005
ISO/IEC 27002
ISO/IEC 27006
ISO/IEC 27701
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 gives purpose and implementation guidance for each of the 93 controls. 27005 is risk management guidance. 27006 sets requirements for certification bodies. 27701 extends the ISMS for privacy information management.

questions.stem: Which statements about ISO/IEC 27002 and ISO/IEC 27005 are correct? Select TWO.
options: ISO/IEC 27005 contains the certifiable requirements for an ISMS
ISO/IEC 27002 gives control-by-control guidance and is not itself a certification standard
ISO/IEC 27002 lists controls that every certified organization must implement
ISO/IEC 27005 gives guidance on managing information security risks
questions.explain: 27002 is guidance for the controls and cannot be certified against; 27005 is risk management guidance. Certifiable ISMS requirements are in 27001, not 27005. No control is universally mandatory; controls are selected through risk treatment.

questions.stem: Put the steps of an ISO/IEC 27001 certification cycle in order.
options: Stage 1 audit reviews ISMS documentation and readiness
Stage 2 audit evaluates whether the ISMS is implemented and effective
The certification body issues the certificate for the defined scope
Surveillance audits sample the ISMS during the certificate cycle
A recertification audit is held before the three-year certificate expires
questions.explain: Stage 1 checks documents and readiness, stage 2 tests implementation, then the certificate is issued. Surveillance audits (normally annual) follow, and recertification renews the three-year cycle.

questions.stem: A company wants an accredited ISO/IEC 27001 certificate it can show to customers. Who carries out the certification audit?
options: An accredited certification body
The company's own internal audit team
The International Organization for Standardization (ISO)
The national standards body that sells copies of the standard
questions.explain: Independent certification bodies, accredited by bodies such as UKAS or JAS-ANZ, perform certification audits. Internal audit is required by clause 9.2 but cannot certify. ISO publishes standards but does not certify organizations, and selling the standard is unrelated to certification.

questions.stem: Which clause of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 requires the organization to determine the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS?
options: Clause 4.3
Clause 5.2
Clause 6.1.2
Clause 8.1
questions.explain: Clause 4.3 covers determining the ISMS scope. Clause 5.2 is the information security policy, 6.1.2 is the risk assessment process, and 8.1 is operational planning and control.

questions.case: A SaaS company is defining its ISMS scope as its customer-facing platform. The platform runs on a public cloud provider, and an outsourced firm handles the service desk and user account requests. The draft scope only lists servers the company itself configures.
questions.stem: What must the company take into account when finalizing the scope?
options: Only the assets it physically owns, since suppliers maintain their own ISMS
The list of Annex A controls it intends to exclude
The results of its most recent internal audit
The interfaces and dependencies between its activities and those performed by other organizations
questions.explain: Clause 4.3 requires the scope to consider internal and external issues, interested-party requirements, and interfaces and dependencies with activities done by others, such as the cloud provider and service desk. Control exclusions belong in the SoA, and internal audit results are not a scope input.

questions.stem: Under clause 5.1, who must demonstrate leadership and commitment to the ISMS?
options: The chief information security officer alone
Top management
The lead internal auditor
The certification body's lead auditor
questions.explain: Clause 5.1 places the requirement on top management, the people who direct and control the organization at the highest level. A CISO can be given ISMS responsibilities under 5.3, but cannot carry top management's accountability. Auditors evaluate the ISMS, they do not lead it.

questions.stem: A draft information security policy is being checked against clause 5.2. Which TWO elements must it contain?
options: Information security objectives or a framework for setting them
A restriction that the policy is shared only with the security team
A commitment to continual improvement of the ISMS
A complete list of the Annex A controls the organization implements
questions.explain: Clause 5.2 requires the policy to include objectives or a framework for setting them and commitments to meet requirements and to continually improve. It must be communicated within the organization, not hidden. The control list belongs in the Statement of Applicability.

questions.stem: Which sub-clause requires the organization to define a risk treatment process that produces a Statement of Applicability?
questions.explain: 6.1.3 defines the risk treatment process, including determining controls, comparing with Annex A, producing the SoA and the risk treatment plan. 6.1.2 is risk assessment, 8.3 implements the treatment plan, and 9.1 is monitoring and measurement.

questions.stem: For each statement about clause 6.1 of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, select Yes if true.

statements.s: The risk assessment process must ensure repeated assessments give consistent, valid and comparable results.
The risk treatment process must produce a Statement of Applicability.
The risk assessment must follow the method described in ISO/IEC 27005 exactly.

questions.explain: 6.1.2 requires consistent, valid and comparable results, and 6.1.3 requires an SoA. 27001 does not mandate a particular method; 27005 is optional guidance the organization may use.

questions.stem: Clause 6.3 was added in the 2022 edition. What does it cover?
options: Planning the internal audit programme
Planning resources for the ISMS
Planning of changes to the ISMS
Planning for ICT readiness for business continuity
questions.explain: Clause 6.3 requires changes to the ISMS to be carried out in a planned manner. Audit programme planning is clause 9.2, resources are clause 7.1, and ICT readiness for business continuity is Annex A control 5.30.

questions.stem: Which characteristics must information security objectives have under clause 6.2? Select THREE.
options: Consistent with the information security policy
Measurable, if practicable
Approved by the certification body
Monitored
Fixed for the full three-year certification cycle
questions.explain: Clause 6.2 requires objectives that are consistent with the policy, measurable if practicable, monitored, communicated and updated as appropriate. Certification bodies do not approve objectives, and objectives should be updated rather than frozen.

questions.stem: Under clause 7.3, people doing work under the organization's control must be aware of what?
options: Every risk recorded in the risk register and its score
The attribute taxonomy used in ISO/IEC 27002
The certification body's audit plan
The information security policy, their contribution to the ISMS, and the implications of not conforming
questions.explain: Clause 7.3 lists awareness of the policy, one's contribution to ISMS effectiveness and the implications of not conforming. Staff do not need full risk register detail, control attributes or the external audit plan.

questions.case: An auditor asks a company how it knows its three network administrators are competent to manage firewall rules. The IT manager says they are 'obviously experienced' but has no records.
questions.stem: What does clause 7.2 require the company to do?
options: Define the competence needed, ensure staff have it, close gaps and retain evidence
Ensure every administrator holds a firewall vendor certification
Provide awareness training only, because competence is not an ISMS clause requirement
Rely on the firewall vendor's support contract as proof of competence
questions.explain: Clause 7.2 requires determining necessary competence, ensuring it via education, training or experience, taking action and evaluating it, and retaining documented information as evidence. No specific certification is mandated, awareness (7.3) is separate, and a vendor contract does not prove staff competence.

questions.stem: What do clauses 8.2 and 8.3 require?
options: Define risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing assessments
Produce the Statement of Applicability
Perform risk assessments at planned intervals or on significant change, and implement the risk treatment plan
Hold management reviews at planned intervals
questions.explain: Clause 8 operates the processes: 8.2 performs risk assessments at planned intervals and on significant change; 8.3 implements the treatment plan. Defining criteria is 6.1.2, producing the SoA is 6.1.3, and management review is 9.3.

questions.case: A retailer outsources payroll processing, which handles employee bank details and is relevant to its ISMS. The ISMS manager proposes removing payroll from all ISMS activities because 'the supplier runs it now'.
questions.stem: What does clause 8.1 of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 require?
options: Outsourced processes are automatically outside the ISMS scope
Externally provided processes, products or services relevant to the ISMS must be controlled
The supplier's ISO/IEC 27001 certificate is sufficient and no further action is needed
Outsourcing must be recorded as a nonconformity under clause 10.2
questions.explain: Clause 8.1 requires the organization to ensure externally provided processes, products or services relevant to the ISMS are controlled. Outsourcing does not remove responsibility. A supplier certificate can support assurance but does not replace control, and outsourcing is not a nonconformity.

questions.stem: Which activity requires top management to review the ISMS at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness?
options: Internal audit (clause 9.2)
Surveillance audit by the certification body
Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation (clause 9.1)
Management review (clause 9.3)
questions.explain: Clause 9.3 management review is performed by top management for suitability, adequacy and effectiveness. Internal audit checks conformity and effective implementation, surveillance audits are external, and 9.1 defines what is measured and how.

questions.stem: For each statement about clause 9 of ISO/IEC 27001:2022, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Internal auditors should be selected to ensure objectivity and impartiality, so they should not audit their own work.
Internal audits only need to check conformity with ISO/IEC 27001, not with the organization's own ISMS requirements.
Evidence of monitoring and measurement results must be available as documented information.

questions.explain: 9.2 requires audits against both the organization's own requirements and 27001, with objective, impartial auditors. 9.1 requires documented information as evidence of the results.

questions.stem: An internal audit finds that former employees still have VPN access. Put the clause 10.2 steps in order.
options: React: control and correct the nonconformity and deal with its consequences
Evaluate the need to eliminate its causes by reviewing it and finding the root cause
Implement the corrective action needed
Review the effectiveness of the corrective action taken
Make changes to the ISMS if necessary
questions.explain: Clause 10.2 expects reaction and correction first, then root-cause evaluation, implementation of action, a review of its effectiveness, and ISMS changes where needed, all kept as documented information.

questions.stem: Which two kinds of risk criteria must the organization establish under ISO/IEC 27001 clause 6.1.2?
options: Recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives
Control effectiveness criteria and audit criteria
Risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing information security risk assessments
Asset valuation criteria and vulnerability scoring criteria
questions.explain: Clause 6.1.2 requires risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing assessments. RTO and RPO are continuity metrics. Audit criteria belong to clause 9.2. Asset values and vulnerability scores may be part of a method but are not the named criteria.

questions.case: Two business units of a university run information security risk assessments. One rates risks as high, medium or low based on judgment; the other uses a 1-25 numeric score. Management cannot tell which risks are the most serious across the university.
questions.stem: Which ISO/IEC 27001 requirement is not being met?
options: Assessments must use a quantitative method expressed in monetary terms
Repeated assessments must produce consistent, valid and comparable results
Each business unit must hold its own certificate
Risk assessments must be performed by the certification body
questions.explain: Clause 6.1.2 requires the risk assessment process to give consistent, valid and comparable results, which needs common criteria. 27001 does not mandate a quantitative or monetary method, certificates are by scope not unit, and the organization itself performs assessments.

questions.stem: Put the information security risk assessment steps of ISO/IEC 27001 in order.
options: Establish risk acceptance criteria and criteria for performing assessments
Identify risks to confidentiality, integrity and availability and their risk owners
Analyse potential consequences and likelihood to determine the level of risk
Evaluate the results against the risk criteria and prioritize risks for treatment
questions.explain: Clause 6.1.2 sets criteria first, then identification (including risk owners), analysis of consequences and likelihood, and evaluation against criteria to prioritize treatment.

questions.stem: A risk analyst has rated a ransomware scenario as likelihood 4 and consequence 5, giving a level of 20. She now compares the score with the organization's thresholds to decide its priority. Which step is she performing?
options: Risk identification
Risk treatment
Risk evaluation
Risk monitoring
questions.explain: Comparing analysed risk levels with risk criteria to prioritize is risk evaluation. Identification finds risks and owners, analysis produced the score of 20, treatment selects options and controls afterwards, and monitoring tracks risks over time.

questions.stem: In ISO/IEC 27001 terms, who is a risk owner?
options: The person or entity with the accountability and authority to manage the risk
The certification body auditor who reviewed the risk
Whoever discovered the threat or vulnerability
The supplier responsible for the affected system
questions.explain: A risk owner has the accountability and authority to manage a risk; risk owners are identified during risk identification and approve the treatment plan. Auditors, discoverers and suppliers do not automatically own risks.

questions.stem: A company buys a cyber insurance policy to cover the financial impact of a data breach. Which risk treatment option is this?
options: Risk avoidance
Risk modification
Risk retention
Risk sharing
questions.explain: Insurance shares part of the risk (mainly financial consequences) with another party. Avoidance stops the activity, modification applies controls to change likelihood or consequence, and retention accepts the risk as it is. Accountability is not transferred.

questions.case: A clinic identifies three risks: a legacy patient portal with unpatchable flaws, staff laptops that could be stolen, and occasional printer outages rated well within its risk acceptance criteria.
questions.stem: Which TWO treatment decisions correctly match the option named?
options: Decommissioning the legacy portal is risk avoidance
Encrypting laptop disks is risk sharing
Formally accepting the printer outage risk is risk retention
Buying insurance for laptops is risk modification
questions.explain: Stopping the activity is avoidance, and knowingly accepting a low risk is retention. Disk encryption is a control, so it is modification, not sharing. Insurance shares the risk rather than modifying it.

questions.stem: Why does ISO/IEC 27001 require the organization to compare its necessary controls with Annex A?
options: To ensure only Annex A controls are used
To verify that no necessary controls have been overlooked
To calculate the residual risk score for each risk
To decide which interested parties are relevant
questions.explain: Clause 6.1.3 uses Annex A as a cross-check to verify no necessary controls were omitted. Controls may come from any source, residual risk is determined by risk analysis after treatment, and interested parties are a clause 4.2 matter.

questions.stem: For each statement about selecting controls under ISO/IEC 27001 clause 6.1.3, select Yes if true.

statements.s: An organization may design its own controls or take them from sources such as NIST or the CIS Controls.
Annex A is an exhaustive list, so a control not in it cannot be part of the ISMS.
A control listed in Annex A is mandatory for every certified organization because it appears there.

questions.explain: Controls come from any source. The standard notes Annex A is not exhaustive and that inclusion in Annex A does not make a control mandatory; controls are included when needed for risk treatment or requirements.

questions.stem: Under ISO/IEC 27001 clause 6.1.3, who must approve the risk treatment plan and accept residual information security risks?
options: The risk owners
The certification body
The internal auditor
The data protection officer
questions.explain: Clause 6.1.3 requires risk owners' approval of the treatment plan and acceptance of residual risks. Certification bodies and internal auditors evaluate the ISMS but do not own risks, and a data protection officer has a privacy role, not general risk ownership.

questions.case: A stage 2 auditor reviews risk R14, 'theft of customer data through compromised remote access'. The risk register shows MFA as the chosen treatment and the SoA marks MFA as implemented. The ISMS manager signed the residual risk acceptance himself because the operations director, who owns the risk, was too busy.
questions.stem: What is the most likely finding?
options: No issue, because the ISMS manager is responsible for the whole ISMS
A nonconformity, because the SoA must not list implemented controls
A nonconformity, because residual risk must be accepted by the risk owner
No issue, because residual risk acceptance is optional when controls are implemented
questions.explain: Clause 6.1.3 requires risk owners to approve the plan and accept residual risk, which links decisions to business accountability. The ISMS manager signing for them does not satisfy this. The SoA must show implementation status, and residual risk acceptance is not optional.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes residual risk?
options: The risk level before any controls are considered
Risk that has been shared with an insurer
Risk that falls outside the ISMS scope
The risk that remains after risk treatment
questions.explain: Residual risk is what remains after treatment and must be accepted by risk owners. The level before controls is often called inherent risk. Shared risk is one treatment option, and out-of-scope risk is a scoping matter.

questions.stem: Which items must a Statement of Applicability contain? Select THREE.
options: The necessary controls and the justification for including them
Whether each necessary control is implemented or not
The full likelihood and consequence score for every risk
Justification for excluding any Annex A control
The names of the certification body's auditors
questions.explain: Clause 6.1.3 d) requires the SoA to list necessary controls with justification for inclusion, whether they are implemented, and justification for excluding Annex A controls. Risk scores belong in the risk register, and auditors' names are not SoA content.

questions.case: A fully remote software company with no offices hosts all systems with a cloud provider. Its draft SoA marks Annex A 7.1 Physical security perimeters as 'excluded' with the justification left blank. Control 7.9 Security of assets off-premises is also excluded because 'we have no premises'.
questions.stem: What is the best advice?
options: Remove 7.1 and 7.9 from the SoA entirely, because excluded controls should not be listed
Exclusions need a real justification; and 7.9 likely still applies because staff laptops are used off-premises
Mark both as implemented, because the cloud provider handles physical security
Exclusions are fine without justification for small organizations
questions.explain: Every excluded Annex A control must stay in the SoA with a justification. With no offices, excluding 7.1 may be justifiable if explained, but laptops used at home are assets off-premises, so 7.9 is probably applicable. Claiming the provider's controls as implemented by the company is inaccurate.

questions.stem: An auditor wants to trace why control 8.13 Information backup is in place and whether it works. Which document links the treated risk to the control and its implementation status?
options: The information security policy
The internal audit programme
The Statement of Applicability
The management review minutes
questions.explain: The SoA records each control's justification (such as a treated risk) and implementation status, linking risk treatment to controls and evidence. The policy states intent, the audit programme schedules audits, and management review minutes record top-level decisions.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Statement of Applicability, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Auditors commonly sample controls marked 'implemented' in the SoA and ask for evidence they operate.
Once the certificate is issued, the SoA should be frozen until recertification.
Controls in the risk treatment plan that are missing from the SoA are a typical audit finding.

questions.explain: The SoA is the auditor's map for sampling evidence. It must be kept current as risks, scope and controls change. Gaps between the risk treatment plan and the SoA are a classic nonconformity.

questions.stem: A payment processor must meet PCI DSS requirements that go beyond Annex A. How should these appear in its ISMS?
options: They cannot be included, because the SoA may list only Annex A controls
They replace Annex A, so the SoA no longer needs to address Annex A controls
They must be certified separately under ISO/IEC 27002
They can be added to the SoA as additional necessary controls with their own justification
questions.explain: 27001 lets controls come from any source, so PCI DSS requirements can be added to the SoA with justification. Every Annex A control must still be included or excluded with reasons. ISO/IEC 27002 is guidance and is not certifiable.

questions.stem: A cloud provider wants additional guidance on cloud-specific information security controls to add to its SoA. Which standard is designed for this?
options: ISO/IEC 27017
ISO/IEC 27005
ISO/IEC 27006
questions.explain: ISO/IEC 27017 is the code of practice for information security controls for cloud services. 27005 is risk management guidance, 27006 sets rules for certification bodies, and ISO 22301 is the business continuity management system standard.

questions.stem: How many controls are in the organizational theme (clause 5) of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A?
questions.explain: Organizational controls number 37 (5.1-5.37). People controls are 8, physical controls are 14, and technological controls are 34, for a total of 93.

questions.stem: A company defines processes for selecting, using, managing and exiting SaaS and IaaS providers according to its security requirements. Which Annex A control does this primarily implement?
options: 8.21 Security of network services
5.23 Information security for use of cloud services
8.30 Outsourced development
5.14 Information transfer
questions.explain: 5.23 covers acquisition, use, management and exit of cloud services. 8.21 secures network services, 8.30 governs outsourced development, and 5.14 covers rules for transferring information.

questions.stem: Which TWO are people controls (Annex A clause 6) in ISO/IEC 27001:2022?
options: Screening
Clear desk and clear screen
Remote working
User endpoint devices
questions.explain: Screening (6.1) and remote working (6.7) are people controls. Clear desk and clear screen is physical (7.7), and user endpoint devices is technological (8.1).

questions.stem: An employee spots a suspicious USB stick in the car park and needs a quick, known way to tell the security team. Which Annex A control addresses this?
options: 5.26 Response to information security incidents
6.4 Disciplinary process
6.8 Information security event reporting
8.16 Monitoring activities
questions.explain: 6.8 requires a mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected security events promptly. 5.26 covers how the organization responds once an incident is declared, 6.4 handles policy violations, and 8.16 is technical monitoring for anomalous behaviour.

questions.stem: A data centre installs CCTV and intrusion alarms that alert guards whenever someone enters a restricted area out of hours. Which control, new in the 2022 edition, does this implement?
options: 7.2 Physical entry
7.1 Physical security perimeters
7.6 Working in secure areas
7.4 Physical security monitoring
questions.explain: 7.4 Physical security monitoring is new in 2022 and requires premises to be continuously monitored for unauthorized physical access. 7.2 controls entry points, 7.1 defines perimeters, and 7.6 covers behaviour inside secure areas.

questions.stem: For each statement about Annex A physical controls, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Clear desk and clear screen is a physical control.
The physical theme contains 14 controls.
Information deletion is a physical control because it concerns storage media.

questions.explain: Clear desk and clear screen is 7.7, and the physical theme has 14 controls. Information deletion is 8.10, a technological control; storage media management is the separate physical control 7.10.

questions.case: A development team requires peer review and approval of every pull request, automated testing, and a rollback plan before any change reaches production.
questions.stem: Which Annex A control best matches this practice?
options: 8.32 Change management
8.9 Configuration management
8.25 Secure development life cycle
8.31 Separation of development, test and production environments
questions.explain: 8.32 requires changes to information processing facilities and systems to follow change management procedures. 8.9 governs secure configurations, 8.25 sets rules for the overall secure development life cycle, and 8.31 keeps environments separate.

questions.stem: Which Annex A theme contains 8.2 Privileged access rights, 8.15 Logging and 8.24 Use of cryptography?
options: Organizational controls
People controls
Technological controls
Physical controls
questions.explain: Controls numbered 8.x belong to the technological theme (34 controls). Organizational controls are 5.x, people controls are 6.x, and physical controls are 7.x.

questions.stem: Which of these controls were NEW in the 2022 edition of Annex A? Select THREE.
options: Data leakage prevention
Protection against malware
Web filtering
Segregation of duties
Secure coding
questions.explain: Data leakage prevention (8.12), web filtering (8.23) and secure coding (8.28) are among the 11 new controls. Protection against malware (8.7) and segregation of duties (5.3) existed in the 2013 edition and were carried forward.

questions.stem: How did the structure of Annex A change from the 2013 edition to the 2022 edition?
options: From 93 controls in 4 themes to 114 controls in 14 domains
From 114 controls in 14 domains to 93 controls in 4 themes
From 133 controls in 11 domains to 114 controls in 14 domains
From 114 controls in 14 domains to 93 controls in 5 cybersecurity functions
questions.explain: The 2013 Annex A had 114 controls in 14 domains; 2022 has 93 controls in four themes (organizational, people, physical, technological). The 133/11 figures are from the 2005 edition, and the five functions (identify, protect, detect, respond, recover) are an attribute, not the grouping.

questions.stem: In ISO/IEC 27002:2022, which values belong to the 'control type' attribute?
options: Identify, protect, detect, respond and recover
Confidentiality, integrity and availability
Governance and ecosystem, protection, defence and resilience
Preventive, detective and corrective
questions.explain: Control type is preventive, detective or corrective. Identify to recover are the cybersecurity concepts attribute, CIA are the information security properties attribute, and governance and ecosystem, protection, defence and resilience are the security domains attribute.

questions.stem: For each statement about control attributes, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Attributes are defined in ISO/IEC 27002 and organizations may also create their own.
Organizational, people, physical and technological are values of the control type attribute.
The cybersecurity concepts attribute aligns with the five functions familiar from the NIST Cybersecurity Framework.

questions.explain: 27002 defines five attributes and allows custom ones. The four themes are the grouping of controls, not attribute values; control type is preventive, detective or corrective. Cybersecurity concepts are identify, protect, detect, respond and recover.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the intended audience of NIST CSF 2.0?
options: Only US federal agencies subject to FISMA
Only owners and operators of US critical infrastructure
Organizations of all sizes and sectors, in any country
Only organizations seeking ISO/IEC 27001 certification
questions.explain: CSF 2.0 broadened its scope to all organizations, of any size or sector, and dropped the old critical-infrastructure title. It is not limited to federal agencies, which follow FISMA and SP 800-53, and it has no link to ISO/IEC 27001 certification.

questions.stem: For each statement about NIST CSF 2.0, select Yes if true.

statements.s: CSF 2.0 was published by NIST in February 2024.
Organizations can be formally certified against CSF 2.0 by accredited certification bodies.
CSF 2.0 applies to technologies including OT, IoT, cloud and AI systems.

questions.explain: CSF 2.0 (NIST CSWP 29) was released on 26 February 2024 and covers all technology types, including OT, IoT, cloud, mobile and AI. It is a voluntary, outcome-based framework with no certification scheme, unlike ISO/IEC 27001.

questions.stem: Which CSF 2.0 component describes an organization's current or target cybersecurity posture in terms of Core outcomes?
options: Organizational Profile
Implementation Tier
Informative Reference
Implementation Example
questions.explain: An Organizational Profile describes current and/or target posture as Core outcomes. Tiers describe how rigorous risk governance and management are. Informative References map outcomes to other standards. Implementation Examples illustrate ways to achieve a Subcategory.

questions.stem: Which THREE are the components of NIST CSF 2.0 as defined in the framework? Select THREE.
options: CSF Core
Statement of Applicability
Organizational Profiles
Tiers
Maturity Model Certification levels
questions.explain: CSF 2.0 has three components: the Core, Organizational Profiles and Tiers. A Statement of Applicability belongs to ISO/IEC 27001. Maturity certification levels come from CMMC, a separate US DoD program, not from the CSF.

questions.stem: How is the CSF 2.0 Core structured?
options: 5 Functions, 23 Categories, 108 Subcategories
6 Functions, 22 Categories, 106 Subcategories
6 Functions, 23 Categories, 108 Subcategories
4 Functions, 22 Categories, 106 Subcategories
questions.explain: CSF 2.0 has 6 Functions (GV, ID, PR, DE, RS, RC), 22 Categories and 106 Subcategories. The figures 5/23/108 describe CSF 1.1, before GOVERN was added. The other combinations mix the two versions.

questions.stem: A reviewer notices that DE.CM jumps from DE.CM-03 to DE.CM-06. What is the most likely explanation?
options: DE.CM-04 and DE.CM-05 are reserved for sector Community Profiles
The missing numbers are optional Subcategories published only online
The gaps mark CSF 1.1 Subcategories that were moved or withdrawn, so their numbers are not reused
DE.CM-04 and DE.CM-05 were merged into the PROTECT Function's PR.PS Category
questions.explain: CSF 2.0 keeps the old identifiers and leaves gaps where 1.1 Subcategories were relocated or withdrawn. There are no reserved slots for Community Profiles and no optional online-only Subcategories. Claiming a specific merger into PR.PS invents a mapping the gap does not indicate.

questions.stem: A consultant tells a client that CSF 2.0 Implementation Examples are the mandatory minimum controls for each Subcategory. How should you respond?
options: Correct: each example must be implemented to claim the outcome
Correct only for organizations operating at Tier 3 or Tier 4
Incorrect: they are the Informative References to SP 800-53, which are mandatory
Incorrect: they are notional, action-oriented illustrations, not a required baseline or checklist
questions.explain: Implementation Examples are notional, action-oriented examples of how an outcome might be reached. NIST says they are not a checklist or required baseline, at any Tier. Informative References are mappings to other standards, and they are not mandatory either.

questions.stem: Why did NIST publish CSF 2.0 Informative References and Implementation Examples online instead of inside the framework document?
options: So they can be updated more frequently than the framework and provided in machine-readable formats
Because they are proprietary and require a paid NIST subscription
Because they apply only to US federal agencies
So that the framework document can serve as a certifiable standard
questions.explain: Keeping them online lets NIST update them more often than the CSF and offer human- and machine-readable formats through the CSF 2.0 Reference Tool. They are free to use, apply to everyone, and the CSF is not a certifiable standard.

questions.stem: Put the CSF 2.0 Tiers in order from least to most rigorous.
options: Partial
Risk Informed
Repeatable
Adaptive
questions.explain: Tier 1 is Partial (ad hoc), Tier 2 is Risk Informed (approved by management), Tier 3 is Repeatable (formal organization-wide policy) and Tier 4 is Adaptive (adapts using lessons learned and predictive indicators).

questions.case: A logistics firm's security practices are approved by its COO and followed by most teams, but no organization-wide cybersecurity policy has been formally adopted. Risk information is shared informally. Leadership wants to know its current Tier.
questions.stem: Which Tier best fits the firm's current cybersecurity risk governance?
options: Tier 1, Partial
Tier 2, Risk Informed
Tier 3, Repeatable
Tier 4, Adaptive
questions.explain: Practices approved by management but not established as organization-wide policy match Tier 2, Risk Informed. Tier 1 is ad hoc. Tier 3 needs formally approved practices expressed as policy. Tier 4 adds organization-wide adaptation and executive monitoring of cyber risk alongside financial risk.

questions.stem: For each statement about CSF Tiers, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Tiers characterize the rigor of an organization's cybersecurity risk governance and management practices.
Every organization is expected to reach Tier 4 to use CSF 2.0 correctly.
An organization can use Tiers to inform its Current and Target Profiles.

questions.explain: Tiers characterize the rigor of risk governance and management, and NIST says they can inform both Profiles. Organizations should choose a Tier that suits their risk and resources. Reaching Tier 4 is not a requirement.

questions.stem: A sector association publishes a baseline set of CSF outcomes that its member manufacturers can adopt as a starting point. What is this called?
options: Organizational Profile
Implementation Tier
Community Profile
Quick-Start Guide
questions.explain: A Community Profile is a published baseline of CSF outcomes for a sector, technology, threat or use case, shared across many organizations. Each member then tailors it into its own Organizational (Target) Profile. A Quick-Start Guide is a short how-to document, and a Tier describes rigor.

questions.stem: A small business with no security staff wants free NIST resources to help it get started with CSF 2.0. Which TWO are the best fit? Select TWO.
options: The CSF 2.0 Small Business Quick-Start Guide
NIST SP 800-53 high baseline
The CSF 2.0 Reference Tool for browsing and exporting the Core
ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A
FedRAMP authorization package templates
questions.explain: Quick-Start Guides, including the Small Business guide, are short, audience-specific starting points, and the CSF 2.0 Reference Tool lets anyone explore and export the Core. The SP 800-53 high baseline and FedRAMP packages target federal systems, and ISO/IEC 27001 is a separate, non-NIST standard.

questions.stem: What does the NIST Cybersecurity and Privacy Reference Tool (CPRT) provide?
options: A certification registry of organizations compliant with CSF 2.0
Reference data from NIST frameworks and guidelines in machine-readable formats such as JSON and XLSX
An automated vulnerability scanner that scores assets against CSF Subcategories
A free SIEM that maps alerts to DE.CM Subcategories
questions.explain: CPRT gives consistent access to reference data from NIST publications, such as the CSF and SP 800-53, in downloadable formats like JSON and XLSX. NIST does not run a CSF certification registry, and CPRT is not a scanner or a SIEM.

questions.stem: Why is GOVERN shown at the centre of the CSF 2.0 Functions wheel?
options: It is the first step and must be completed before the other Functions begin
It is the only Function that applies to small businesses
It replaces the IDENTIFY Function from CSF 1.1
It informs how an organization implements the other five Functions
questions.explain: NIST places GOVERN at the centre because it informs how the other five Functions are implemented. The Functions are addressed concurrently, not in sequence, so GOVERN is not a step to finish first. All Functions apply to every organization, and IDENTIFY still exists in CSF 2.0.

questions.stem: A company documents its obligations under privacy law and customer contracts so they shape cybersecurity decisions. Which CSF 2.0 Category does this support?
options: GV.PO Policy
GV.OC Organizational Context
GV.OV Oversight
ID.RA Risk Assessment
questions.explain: GV.OC-03 covers understanding and managing legal, regulatory and contractual cyber requirements, including privacy obligations. GV.PO sets the organization's own policy, GV.OV reviews whether the strategy is working, and ID.RA assesses threats and vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: Which TWO outcomes belong to GV.RM Risk Management Strategy? Select TWO.
options: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated and maintained
Hardware inventories are maintained
Cybersecurity risk management activities are included in enterprise risk management processes
Incidents are categorized and prioritized
Personnel receive awareness training
questions.explain: GV.RM-02 sets risk appetite and tolerance, and GV.RM-03 brings cyber risk into ERM. Hardware inventories are ID.AM-01, incident categorization is RS.MA-03, and awareness training is PR.AT-01.

questions.stem: An internal audit finds that HR does not tell IT when staff leave, so accounts stay active. Which CSF 2.0 Subcategory most directly covers building cybersecurity into these HR processes?
options: GV.RR-04
PR.AT-01
GV.PO-01
DE.CM-03
questions.explain: GV.RR-04 states that cybersecurity is included in human resources practices, such as onboarding, role changes and offboarding. PR.AT-01 is awareness training, GV.PO-01 sets overall policy, and DE.CM-03 monitors personnel activity. None of those addresses the HR process gap.

questions.stem: For each statement about GOVERN, select Yes if true.

statements.s: GV.RR-01 makes organizational leadership responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk.
GV.RR-03 covers allocating adequate resources in line with the risk strategy, roles and policies.
GV.RR is the Category that maintains inventories of supplier-provided services.

questions.explain: GV.RR-01 puts accountability on leadership, and GV.RR-03 covers adequate resourcing. Inventories of supplier-provided services are ID.AM-04 under IDENTIFY, not part of GV.RR.

questions.stem: Each quarter, the risk committee reviews security KPIs and the results of the cyber strategy, then adjusts direction where targets are missed. Which Category is this?
options: GV.PO Policy
GV.RM Risk Management Strategy
GV.OV Oversight
ID.IM Improvement
questions.explain: GV.OV uses the results of risk management activities to review and adjust strategy and evaluate performance (GV.OV-01 and GV.OV-03). GV.RM sets the strategy, and GV.PO establishes and maintains policy. ID.IM finds operational improvements from evaluations, tests and exercises, not strategy-level oversight.

questions.stem: A new regulation takes effect and the company revises its cybersecurity policy and re-communicates it to staff. Which Subcategory does this satisfy?
options: GV.OV-02
GV.PO-02
GV.OC-01
PR.AT-02
questions.explain: GV.PO-02 covers reviewing, updating, communicating and enforcing the policy as requirements, threats, technology and mission change. GV.OV-02 reviews the strategy, GV.OC-01 is understanding the mission, and PR.AT-02 trains specialized roles.

questions.case: A hospital is replacing its cloud-hosted patient scheduling vendor. The new vendor will hold patient data. The old vendor's contract ends in 60 days. The CISO wants to map the work to CSF 2.0 supply chain outcomes.
questions.stem: Which TWO GV.SC Subcategories most directly apply to this transition? Select TWO.
options: GV.SC-06: planning and due diligence before entering the new relationship
GV.SC-10: activities after the old partnership or agreement ends
GV.OC-01: the mission is understood
PR.DS-02: data in transit is protected
GV.RR-04: cybersecurity in HR practices
questions.explain: Vetting the new vendor before signing is GV.SC-06. Making sure the old vendor returns or destroys patient data and loses access after the contract ends is GV.SC-10. GV.OC-01, PR.DS-02 and GV.RR-04 are real outcomes, but they are not supply chain lifecycle outcomes.

questions.stem: Which GV.SC Subcategory covers writing cybersecurity requirements into supplier contracts?
options: GV.SC-04
GV.SC-07
GV.SC-09
GV.SC-05
questions.explain: GV.SC-05 sets requirements for addressing cyber risk in the supply chain and includes them in contracts and agreements. GV.SC-04 ranks suppliers by criticality, GV.SC-07 assesses and monitors supplier risk through the relationship, and GV.SC-09 integrates practices across the product lifecycle.

questions.stem: A team diagrams which systems are authorized to communicate and how customer data flows to external partners. Which Subcategory does this support?
options: ID.AM-03
ID.AM-01
PR.IR-01
DE.CM-01
questions.explain: ID.AM-03 maintains representations of authorized network communication and internal and external data flows. ID.AM-01 is the hardware inventory, PR.IR-01 protects networks from unauthorized access, and DE.CM-01 monitors networks for adverse events.

questions.stem: For each statement about ID.AM, select Yes if true.

statements.s: ID.AM-08 covers managing systems, hardware, software, services and data throughout their life cycles.
ID.AM-05 prioritizes assets based on classification, criticality, resources and impact on the mission.
ID.AM-07 covers monitoring personnel activity for adverse events.

questions.explain: ID.AM-08 is life cycle management and ID.AM-05 is asset prioritization. ID.AM-07 maintains inventories of data and its metadata. Monitoring personnel activity is DE.CM-03.

questions.stem: After a ransomware tabletop exercise with its managed service provider, a company records lessons learned and updates its incident response plan. Which CSF 2.0 Category covers this?
options: RS.AN Incident Analysis
ID.IM Improvement
RC.RP Incident Recovery Plan Execution
GV.OV Oversight
questions.explain: ID.IM, new in CSF 2.0, identifies improvements from tests and exercises, including those with suppliers (ID.IM-02), and maintains IR plans (ID.IM-04). RS.AN investigates real incidents, RC.RP runs recovery, and GV.OV reviews strategy performance.

questions.stem: Before deploying network switches from a new supplier, a company checks that the firmware is genuine and has not been tampered with. Which Subcategory is this?
options: PR.PS-03
GV.SC-04
ID.RA-09
DE.CM-09
questions.explain: ID.RA-09 assesses the authenticity and integrity of hardware and software before acquisition and use. PR.PS-03 covers maintaining and replacing hardware, GV.SC-04 ranks suppliers by criticality, and DE.CM-09 monitors computing assets once they are in operation.

questions.stem: Quarterly access reviews remove excessive permissions so that users keep only what their job needs. Which Subcategory does this map to?
options: PR.AA-01
PR.AA-03
PR.AA-06
PR.AA-05
questions.explain: PR.AA-05 covers defining, managing, enforcing and reviewing access permissions under least privilege and separation of duties. PR.AA-01 manages identities and credentials, PR.AA-03 authenticates users, services and hardware, and PR.AA-06 manages physical access.

questions.stem: For each statement about PROTECT, select Yes if true.

statements.s: Giving database administrators role-specific security training maps to PR.AT-02.
Badge-controlled entry to the server room is managed under PR.AA-06.
PR.AA-04 covers training all staff to recognize phishing.

questions.explain: PR.AT-02 trains specialized roles, and PR.AA-06 manages physical access. PR.AA-04 protects, conveys and verifies identity assertions. General phishing awareness for all staff is PR.AT-01.

questions.stem: An engineer enables audit logging on all servers so that logs are available to the SOC. Which CSF 2.0 Subcategory does enabling the logs fall under?
options: PR.PS-04
DE.CM-09
DE.AE-03
ID.AM-02
questions.explain: PR.PS-04 covers generating log records and making them available for continuous monitoring. Watching those logs is DE.CM-09, and correlating them is DE.AE-03. ID.AM-02 is the software and systems inventory.

questions.stem: Which TWO Subcategories belong to PR.DS Data Security? Select TWO.
options: Backups are created, protected, maintained and tested
Installation of unauthorized software is prevented
Confidentiality, integrity and availability of data in use are protected
Configuration management practices are applied
Networks are protected from unauthorized logical access
questions.explain: Backups (PR.DS-11) and data in use (PR.DS-10) are both PR.DS outcomes. Blocking unauthorized software (PR.PS-05) and configuration management (PR.PS-01) are Platform Security. Network protection from unauthorized logical access is PR.IR-01.

questions.stem: A data centre installs fire suppression, flood sensors and backup generators to protect its servers. Which Subcategory is the best fit?
options: PR.AA-06
PR.IR-02
DE.CM-02
PR.DS-11
questions.explain: PR.IR-02 protects technology assets from environmental threats. PR.AA-06 controls physical access, DE.CM-02 monitors the physical environment for adverse events, and PR.DS-11 covers backups.

questions.stem: A SIEM links a suspicious VPN login with unusual file access and firewall alerts from three different systems. Which Subcategory describes this activity?
options: DE.CM-01
RS.AN-03
DE.AE-03
ID.RA-02
questions.explain: DE.AE-03 correlates information from multiple sources. DE.CM-01 monitors networks to generate events in the first place. RS.AN-03 determines root cause after an incident is declared, and ID.RA-02 is receiving threat intelligence for risk assessment.

questions.stem: Which CSF 2.0 Subcategory covers formally declaring an incident when adverse events meet defined criteria?
options: RS.MA-01
RS.MA-02
DE.AE-04
DE.AE-08
questions.explain: DE.AE-08 declares incidents when adverse events meet the incident criteria. RS.MA-01 then executes the IR plan, and RS.MA-02 triages and validates reports. DE.AE-04 estimates impact and scope.

questions.stem: Which TWO activities are DE.CM Continuous Monitoring outcomes? Select TWO.
options: Monitoring a cloud provider's administrative activity on your tenant
Integrating threat intelligence into event analysis
Monitoring CCTV and door sensors for unusual physical activity
Containing a compromised host
Generating log records on servers
questions.explain: Monitoring external service providers is DE.CM-06, and monitoring the physical environment is DE.CM-02. Integrating threat intelligence into analysis is DE.AE-07, containment is RS.MI-01, and generating logs is PR.PS-04.

questions.stem: Put these CSF 2.0 outcomes in order as a malware incident moves from detection to recovery.
options: Declare the incident because events meet defined criteria (DE.AE-08)
Execute the incident response plan (RS.MA-01)
Contain the incident (RS.MI-01)
Eradicate the incident (RS.MI-02)
Execute the recovery portion of the plan (RC.RP-01)
questions.explain: DETECT declares the incident (DE.AE-08), RESPOND activates the IR plan (RS.MA-01), contains the spread (RS.MI-01) and then eradicates the cause (RS.MI-02), and RECOVER executes the recovery portion of the plan (RC.RP-01).

questions.case: During a breach investigation, analysts image three servers, record hashes of each image and log every action they take. Legal counsel says the evidence may be used in court and must show who handled it and when.
questions.stem: Which CSF 2.0 Category most directly covers these activities?
options: RS.AN Incident Analysis
DE.AE Adverse Event Analysis
RS.MI Incident Mitigation
ID.RA Risk Assessment
questions.explain: RS.AN-06 and RS.AN-07 record investigation actions and collect incident data while preserving integrity and provenance, which is chain of custody. DE.AE analyzes events before declaration, RS.MI contains and eradicates, and ID.RA assesses risk in advance.

questions.stem: The SOC isolates an infected workstation from the network using EDR. Which Subcategory is this?
options: RS.MI-02
RC.RP-02
RS.MI-01
PR.IR-01
questions.explain: Isolating the host contains the incident, which is RS.MI-01. Removing the malware afterwards is eradication (RS.MI-02). RC.RP-02 performs recovery actions, and PR.IR-01 is preventive network protection, not incident response.

questions.stem: Within the required deadline, a company notifies its privacy regulator and affected customers about a data breach under investigation. Which Subcategory is this?
options: RC.CO-03
RS.CO-02
GV.OC-03
DE.AE-06
questions.explain: RS.CO-02 notifies internal and external stakeholders of incidents during response. RC.CO-03 communicates recovery progress. GV.OC-03 is knowing the legal requirements in advance, and DE.AE-06 passes event information to authorized staff and tools.

questions.stem: Put these RC.RP recovery outcomes in a logical order for restoring a ransomware-hit file server.
options: Execute the recovery portion of the incident response plan
Verify the integrity of backups before using them
Restore services and verify the integrity of restored assets
Declare the end of recovery and complete documentation
questions.explain: RC.RP-01 starts recovery, RC.RP-03 checks that backups are clean before use, RC.RP-05 restores and verifies systems and confirms normal status, and RC.RP-06 declares the end of recovery against criteria and completes documentation.

questions.case: After a ransomware outage, a retailer's systems are being restored. Customers are posting on social media and the press is asking questions. The CEO wants regular public updates, but legal wants every message pre-approved.
questions.stem: Which CSF 2.0 Subcategory best addresses sharing these public updates?
options: RS.CO-03
GV.RM-05
RC.RP-04
RC.CO-04
questions.explain: RC.CO-04 shares public updates on incident recovery using approved methods and messaging. RS.CO-03 shares information with designated stakeholders during response, GV.RM-05 sets risk communication lines in advance, and RC.RP-04 sets post-incident operational norms.

questions.stem: For each statement about how the CSF 2.0 Functions operate, select Yes if true.

statements.s: NIST says the Functions should be addressed concurrently.
An organization must fully complete IDENTIFY before it starts any PROTECT activities.
RESPOND and RECOVER capabilities should be ready at all times, even when no incident is underway.

questions.explain: CSF 2.0 says the Functions should be addressed concurrently. GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT and DETECT happen continuously, and RESPOND and RECOVER should be ready at all times and run when incidents occur. There is no requirement to finish one Function first.

questions.case: Midway through a breach, the email service is being restored from backup while analysts still hunt for attacker persistence on other hosts, and the CISO briefs the board on residual risk.
questions.stem: For each statement about this scenario, select Yes if true.
questions.explain: Restoring from backup is RECOVER (RC.RP), and briefing the board on risk is GOVERN (GV.OV and GV.RR). NIST says the Functions are addressed concurrently and DETECT is continuous. Pausing monitoring during recovery would give a persistent attacker room to return.

statements.s: Restoring the email service from backup is a RECOVER activity.
Because recovery has started, DETECT monitoring should be paused until it finishes.
Briefing the board on residual cyber risk is a GOVERN activity.

questions.stem: Put the CSF 2.0 steps for creating and using an Organizational Profile in order.
options: Scope the Organizational Profile
Gather the information needed to prepare the Profile
Create the Organizational Profile
Analyze gaps between Current and Target Profiles and create an action plan
Implement the action plan and update the Profile
questions.explain: NIST's five steps are: scope, gather information, create the Profile (Current and Target), analyze gaps and build a prioritized action plan, then implement and update. The cycle repeats as conditions change.

questions.stem: A company has completed its Current and Target Profiles. What should it produce next?
options: A Statement of Applicability for certification
A Community Profile for its sector
A gap analysis and a prioritized action plan, such as a risk register or POA&M
A Tier 4 attestation letter from NIST
questions.explain: Step 4 analyzes the gaps between Current and Target and builds a prioritized action plan, often recorded in a risk register or POA&M. An SoA belongs to ISO/IEC 27001, Community Profiles are sector baselines, and NIST issues no attestations.

questions.stem: For each statement about Organizational Profiles, select Yes if true.

statements.s: A Profile can be scoped to a single business unit, system or product line rather than the whole organization.
A Community Profile can serve as a starting point for an organization's Target Profile.
A Target Profile describes only the outcomes the organization already achieves today.

questions.explain: Profiles can be scoped narrowly, and a Community Profile can seed a Target Profile. The outcomes achieved today are the Current Profile. The Target Profile holds the desired outcomes the organization has selected and prioritized.

questions.stem: Following the NIST IR 8286 series, put the flow of cybersecurity risk information in order, from the most detailed level to executive oversight.
options: System-level cybersecurity risk register (CSRR)
Organization-level aggregated CSRR
Enterprise risk register (ERR)
Enterprise risk profile (ERP) reviewed by leadership
